results.title: Albania's youth are protesting in Flamingo Revolution, not leaving the country anymore
results.content: Youth protests against a rigid political system and corruption have shaken the government of Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama. They also show that fewer young people are willing to emigrate in search of a better future.

results.title: Saudi pop music is thriving — but for the right reasons?
results.content: As part of Vision 2030, Saudi Arabia's music scene has evolved hugely thanks to state funding and support. Local musicians and DJs are optimistic. But are they actually just helping prop up an authoritarian state?

results.title: Protests in Iraqi Kurdistan at plans for government in Baghdad to take over oil, border crossings
results.content: Thousands have gathered in the capital of northern Iraq's semiautonomous Kurdish region, waving flags and voicing opposition to plans for the federal government to take control of oil operations and border crossings.

results.title: Is authoritarian Vietnam ready to phase out the death penalty?
results.content: Vietnam has voted to abolish the death penalty for six more crimes, continuing a decades-long trend of restricting capital punishment.

results.title: Africa's opposition voices face growing pressure
results.content: Opposition politicians and government critics say arrests, prosecutions and restrictions on public activity are making it harder to challenge those in power. Is a broader pattern emerging?

results.title: FIFA says a cyberattack against it targeted a 'limited set of personal and business information'
results.content: World football's governing body says the cyberattack targeted personal and business information. They struck at a sensitive time for the under-fire organization and its president, Gianni Infantino.

results.title: EU-Indonesia trade deal opens new markets, but challenges remain
results.content: The agreement offers new export and investment opportunities for Jakarta and Brussels. But can Indonesia turn Europe's growing interest in its markets and critical minerals into sustainable gains at home?

results.title: Crew member dies after diesel tanker sinks off Ibiza coast
results.content: Authorities rescued 17 crew members but one later died in hospital after a diesel tanker capsized off the Spanish island of Ibiza. A contingency plan against possible pollution damage is now in place.

results.title: Russia-Ukraine war extends to the Baltic and the Mediterranean
results.content: By attacking Russian vessels around the world, Kyiv is trying to up the pressure on Moscow and also sending out signals to its Western allies. What is the impact on global maritime trade?

results.title: How Chinese companies circumvent chips sanctions in Southeast Asia
results.content: High-tech AI chips are hard to get in China because of US restrictions. To get around this, Chinese companies often use offshore computing capacity, particularly in Southeast Asia. The US is also trying to stop it.

results.title: Can Rassvet, 'Russia's Starlink' change the course of the war in Ukraine?
results.content: SpaceX's US Starlink satellite system has played a key role in countering the Russian military in Ukraine, but now a Russian counterpart is under development. What could this mean for Ukraine?

results.title: Peter Magyar meets Volodymyr Zelenskyy: Hungary and Ukraine make a fresh start after the icy relations of the Viktor Orban era
results.content: After years of frosty and hostile relations under Hungary's Kremlin-friendly former PM Viktor Orban, his successor, Peter Magyar, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy seek to reset their countries' ties.
